semantic_correction.stem: A nurse sees the medication names hydrALAZINE and hydrOXYzine displayed with selected uppercase letters. What is the purpose of this Tall Man lettering?

options.A: To make differences between look-alike drug names more noticeable and reduce name confusion.
options.B: To indicate that both medications require the same administration schedule.
options.C: To identify medications that must be stored under the same conditions.
options.D: To show that both medications belong to the same pharmacologic class.

semantic_correction.rationale: FDA describes Tall Man lettering as the use of uppercase letters to help differentiate look-alike drug names by highlighting dissimilar letters. FDA's current Name Differentiation Project specifically lists hydralazine and hydroxyzine as hydrALAZINE and hydrOXYzine. Therefore, option A states the purpose of the lettering. The capitalization does not indicate dosing schedule, storage requirements, or pharmacologic class.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize Tall Man lettering as a medication-safety strategy that highlights differences between look-alike drug names to reduce name confusion.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original correct answer was uniquely longest and the item was mapped to Safety/Infection. FDA directly supports both the purpose of Tall Man lettering and this exact name pair; the revised item uses parallel distractors and the medication-safety blueprint domain.

option_audit.A: Correct. FDA states that Tall Man lettering highlights dissimilar letters in look-alike names to make name differences more apparent.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Tall Man capitalization does not communicate a shared dosing schedule.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Tall Man capitalization does not encode storage requirements.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Tall Man capitalization does not indicate shared pharmacologic class.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. Only A describes the FDA-defined purpose of Tall Man lettering.
cueing_check: All four choices are parallel statements explaining the capitalization and are comparable in length; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
